reason: The cited evidence does not provide specific prior results supporting the key premises. E1 discusses general complexity and limitations of CPA but offers no data on HfNbTaTiZr or separate transport channels. E2 addresses powder metallurgy and oxygen contamination, not thermal transport. E3 describes phonon linewidth modeling challenges and force-constant fluctuations in a different context, without validating the proposed ML-DFT approach or the claimed equal contributions below 200 K.
premises: Lattice and electronic thermal conductivities in HfNbTaTiZr can be separately calculated and summed to match total measured values.
Machine-learned force fields can capture complex force-constant fluctuations for phonon transport.
DFT-based Boltzmann transport can accurately compute electronic thermal conductivity.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic contributions are nearly equal in defect-free HfNbTaTiZr.
High-temperature total conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr is 10–17 W/(K m).
